oneLiner: Using AI to predict biochemistry for manufacturing and therapeutics
description:
The next decade is going to see a biotech revolution fueled by three technologies: ability to read DNA (sequencing), ability to write DNA (synthesis), and computational systems that predict what DNA to read and write. With sequencing and synthesis being mainstream now [1], 20n provides the computational systems that predict DNA design for novel industrial biotech and health applications.

At 20n, we are taking a fresh look at turning biological data into information. We approach it as a big data learning problem, and bring to bear techniques from machine learning, distributed systems, AI planning, program synthesis, data mining, and natural language processing. With the support of DARPA [2], we are building a team of computer scientists, and bioengineers to look at biology in fundamentally new ways.

Our current customers include industrial biotech firms that are leading the charge in transitioning us from traditional unsustainable means of manufacturing to sustainable biological processes leading to advanced fuels, materials, therapeutics, and flavors and fragrances. 20n’s technology helps them enter markets previously thought inaccessible for biology.

[1] Sequencing DNA costs $4k/genome (http://www.genome.gov/sequencingcosts/) and is expected to go down to $1k/genome. Synthesizing DNA is at 20cents/bp, and is expected to go down to 0.1cents/bp.
[2] DARPA in the past supported work that led to the internet, stealth planes, GPS, and even Douglas Engelbart’s mother-of-all-demos.

oneLiner: India's only full-stack financial solutions company for businesses.
description:
The journey of building Razorpay started in 2014, when Harshil Mathur (CEO & Co-Founder) and Shashank Kumar (MD & Co-Founder) witnessed the dismal state of the online payments industry in India then and understood that they have a larger and more important issue to solve. And That was democratizing online payments for Indian businesses, particularly the underserved market, Startups and SMEs. Over the last 9 years, Razorpay has evolved from a single-product company to a multi-product company, from an online payment gateway to India’s only full-stack financial solutions company, offering payments and banking solutions to businesses.  Razorpay today is transforming age-old complexities and changing every known paradigm of money movement for disruptive businesses.

Over the last couple of years, Razorpay’s growth has evolved to be an index of India’s digital economy. From a kirana shop in Kashmir collecting payments on our POS device to a textile exporter in Kanyakumari accepting dollars through our International Payments product, Razorpay has revolutionised how businesses have traditionally transacted and interacted with money. 

Razorpay became the first and only Indian fintech to build a full-stack international Payment Gateway ‘Curlec by Razorpay’ and evolved into a comprehensive provider of payment solutions, leveraging the synergy between cutting-edge technological capabilities and a profound understanding of the local payment ecosystem. The introduction of the new Curlec Payment Gateway aims to cater to a wide spectrum of businesses, expanding its reach to over 5,000 establishments. 

Be it for international expansion or solving for Indian businesses, for Razorpay, the customer has always been at the core of all disruption, from addressing evolving needs to delivering new solutions. This hyperfocus helped bring Razorpay’s several industry-first innovations into the market since 2014. Razorpay became the first to launch a completely digital on-boarding process for startups, first to launch support for UPI, first to launch support for Bharath QR, first to introduce recurring payments for businesses through Razorpay Route, automating payment receipts and later automate payouts and making the entire process seamless and optimized and many more were introduced aling the way. Other firsts include: - First to launch India’s Multi-Network Tokenisation solution, TokenHQ - Razorpay became India’s first payment gateway to support credit cards on UPI - Razorpay also became India’s largest omnichannel payment gateway for businesses post acquiring Ezetap which is India’s leading offline POS company that was founded with the aim to simplify the in-person offline payments experience.

Over the years, Razorpay’s valuation has jumped from $1 billion to $7.5 billion and has added a host of marquee investors to its captable. Razorpay is also the second Indian company to be a part of Silicon Valley’s largest tech accelerator, Y Combinator. Marquee investors such as Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital, TCV, GIC, Tiger Global, Sequoia Capital India, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, Salesforce Ventures, Y Combinator, and MasterCard have invested a total of $741.5 Mn through Series A, B, C, D, E and F funding. The last financing round of Series F led the company’s valuation to $7.5 Billion signaling one of the fastest increases in valuation for an Indian Unicorn. 

Razorpay has also made acquisitions with like-minded companies over the last 9 years. In total, till date, Razorpay has made eight acquisitions, Billme in 2023 - A Digital invoice and customer Engagement, Ezetap in 2022 - India’s leading offline POS company, PoshVine in 2022 - India’s leading loyalty and reward management platform, IZealiant in 2022 - A mobile-first, API-enabled, and cloud-ready payment solution and made its first international foray in South-East Asia by announcing its acquisition of Curlec in 2022 - A recurring payments platform. TeraFin Labs in 2021 - the AI-based SaaS platform that facilitates digital financing solutions, Opfin (Now RazorpayX Payroll) in 2019 -  The payroll management solution and Thirdwatch in 2019, the first acquisition - The AI-powered fraud detection platform.

All these efforts are being done in collaboration with banks, regulators, and stakeholders so that India can build a better place for small and big businesses. Today, Razorpay powers online payments for 76 Of 100 startup unicorns and millions of businesses in India. The core premise of what Razorpay was founded in 2014 and what it is today hasn’t changed. It is to make money movement simpler and easier, whether it is for businesses to receive money, send money, or manage money.

oneLiner: Automatic Data Extraction
description:
AI agents break where it matters most: when the details are buried in an invoice, a BoL, or a clinical document. Most agents guess. They hallucinate field values, apply rules inconsistently, and when something goes wrong, you can’t tell why or fix it without redoing the work yourself.

Nanonets is built differently. Every extraction is traceable. You can see exactly what the agent read, what rule it applied, and why it made the call it did. When it’s uncertain, it flags the right thing for human review instead of silently getting it wrong. When you correct it, it learns. When you add business rules, it tracks which rule drove which decision.

Anyone can build agentic workflows, but AI agents are black boxes that struggle with complex files and processes, like POs, invoices, BoLs and clinical documents. Nanonets agents understand key details in files, work through complex processes and act with transparency, making them the most reliable foundation for building workflows where details matter.

Nanonets reduces processing time by 95% by automating messy manual processes and delivering clean data to systems of record like SAP, SFDC and more. That’s why Nanonets is the automation layer global enterprises reach for when accuracy is non-negotiable.

oneLiner: The neural engine for autonomous robots
description:
We aren’t building AI to replace "knowledge work” that requires neither, but to bolster the working human intellect which has never failed to discover new paths to prosperity.

For all their success, mainstream approaches to AI have fundamental limitations preventing them from solving critical classes of problems. We are building a new AI architecture from first principles to break from these limitations.

The status quo has ossified around the supervised, brute-force pretraining paradigm. These systems do not, and cannot, handle the essential skills of continual learning, goal discovery, novel planning, and the creation of new knowledge.

These limitations are not trivial. Our national prosperity depends directly on overcoming these limitations, because the essential skills underlie the skilled trades. From electricians to machinists to nurses, apprentice tradespeople in all of these fields learn “skilled improvisation” where every solution is novel, and even the goal must be discovered. Prosperity demands the precise capabilities where status quo AI is structurally weak.

Worse, these limitations will not be overcome with more compute or training data. They are inescapable consequences of the underlying technologies of supervised learning, neural networks, transformers, backprop, and gradient descent. Progress requires independence from them.

We are building a new AI architecture by reverse-engineering the system that got us this far: the human brain. By triangulating between neuroscience, cognitive science, and the evolutionary elaboration of brains, we have identified the brain’s algorithms to (a) continually learn a causal world model (b) select goals to both achieve and learn to achieve more (c) plan to reach novel goals, and (d) creatively produce new knowledge.


Join us in building intelligence with ingenuity to bolster the skilled trades.

In addition, logistics operators are under huge sustainability pressure, as Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs) are responsible for 16% of the UK's transport emissions but only 5% of the miles travelled. While electric vehicle sales for passenger vehicles are on the rise, the same can't be said for long-haul HGVs due to high initial cost and limited range, making it impractical for logistic purposes. 

With this problem in mind, we aim to leverage the latest AI techniques to improve the fuel efficiency of diesel trucks today, and increase the range of zero-emission trucks of the future. 

Our product Hypermile Co-Pilot is a retrofittable AI cruise control for commercial vehicles focused on controlling the speed of the truck efficiently. We have trained the AI algorithms to learn the best techniques for saving fuel: anticipating how traffic flow will change, optimising speed based on the road gradient and maximizing vehicle coasting. As a result, we can reduce diesel consumption by 11% and extend the range of battery-electric vehicles by 15%. The long term vision is to incrementally build higher levels of autonomy with the next milestone being a Level-3 autonomous trucking solution. 

The company was founded in May 2020 and raised a $1.5M pre-seed round in May 2021 from Y Combinator, Greg Brockman (CTO of OpenAI), Luc Vincent (former Executive VP of Autonomous Driving at Lyft Level 5) and others. We’ve received a number of R&D grants from Innovate UK, Department for Transport and Horizons 2020. 3. **Flexible Data Management**: We understand that data privacy is critical. Helicone supports deployment options for dedicated instances, hybrid cloud integrations, or self-hosted environments, allowing clients to maintain control over their data and ensuring compliance with privacy standards.

### Built for Developers and Data Scientists

Helicone is designed to meet the needs of engineers and data scientists who require transparency and control over their LLMs. From chatbots to document processing systems, Helicone equips you with the insights needed to track costs, understand user interactions, and optimize outputs—all from one intuitive platform.

By combining observability with LLM-specific insights, Helicone is redefining AI monitoring, empowering developers to deploy and scale their AI models with confidence.

oneLiner: Radar: the missing Kubernetes interface for humans and agents
description:
Radar is the missing open-source Kubernetes interface for humans and agents.

Kubernetes is easy to query, but hard to understand. Radar shows what's failing in a cluster, why, and what changed: issues and root cause, topology, an event and change timeline, Helm, GitOps (Argo CD and Flux), traffic, image internals, audits, upgrade impact and CVEs. Engineers get a UI. AI agents get a built-in MCP server with structured cluster context instead of raw YAML, and Radar can run AI investigations through the agent CLI you already use (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode).

Radar is and always will be open source: a single Apache 2.0 binary that runs on your laptop against your kubeconfig, or in-cluster via Helm, with no agents or CRDs to install. 4.2k+ GitHub stars.

Radar Cloud keeps watching when you close the laptop: grouped alerts to Slack, AI investigations with evidence on alerts or on demand, fleet-wide issues, search and diffs across every cluster behind one MCP endpoint, 30 days of history, and shared views scoped by Kubernetes RBAC. SOC 2 on every plan; SSO, SCIM and self-managed on Enterprise.

Radar is built by Skyhook. Get started at https://radarhq.io or https://github.com/skyhook-io/radar

oneLiner: The AI Support Agent for Ecommerce

## What is Yuma AI?

Yuma is automating customer support by providing an AI Support Agent orchestration platform. Yuma provides autonomous AI agents dedicated to customer service and e-commerce.

We integrate directly with help desk software (Zendesk, Kustomer, Gorgias, etc.) and focus on helping large Shopify brands deal with their high volume of support requests.

Top merchants using Yuma can automate up to 80% of their support tickets fully autonomously.

## Why do Shopify merchants need Yuma?

There are thousands of large Shopify merchants around the world generating $10M+ a year. Most of them have taken over some niches and are great at what they do: selling their products.

But they all have one thing in common: they all hate customer support. It's a burden for them and a huge source of cost, as they receive hundreds of requests per day. Some of them have dozens of support agents on staff, usually offshore, and the overall quality is still often pretty poor while staff turnover remains high.

Those merchants have been promised automation for years but have always been disappointed by the outcome. As customers, we have all had to live through a terrible support automation experience before, so this is no secret, and everyone knows that the current state of the technology is quite bad.

## Yuma is solving this in a few ways:

Yuma isn't just another RAG chatbot. Our platform provides autonomous AI agents dedicated to support and ecommerce.

These agents are powered by knowledge, follow processes, and are managed by our in-house AI orchestration technology. This ensures safety, control, and quality at every step.

We believe that to truly automate customer support, we must develop a platform that mimics the actions of a human support agent. That's exactly what we've been doing.

Currently, our top merchants are automating 60% of their support tickets through Yuma. Yuma can fetch information from external services and take actions in other apps as needed to resolve each ticket.

We are laser-focused on building the best AI support agent platform and aim to achieve 80% true automation in the next few months.

## Fun Fact

Yuma got started by accident. This is my third YC startup after Socialcam (W12) and Triplebyte (S15). I released Yuma as a prototype for fun in mid-December 2022 and was overwhelmed with demo requests. That's when I knew I was onto something and had to turn this into a real company, once again.

2) Why should I pick Redis over Milvus as my underlying vector store?
3) Does this codebase in our organization still work and what steps are required for a complex integration with another library?

Sage’s answers are directly supported by documentation and external references like GitHub, Stack Overflow, technical design documents, and project management software, preventing hallucinations. We have 20+ years of software engineering and AI research experience. Julia worked on precursors of Gemini using contextual neural techniques before they were called “RAG” (and applied it to products like Google Keyboard and Pixel phones). oneLiner: Powerful quantitative forecasting models
description:
Historically, quantitative models are domain specific. Brilliant people spend their best years testing features, tuning hyperparameters, and iterating architectures within a narrow domain. But scale is the panacea: large models will find patterns people, and specialized models, could not. 

Forecasting generalizes. Zoa trains cross-domain event forecasting engines. 

*Automating Iteration*

LLMs—embedded in multi-agent optimization loops and evaluated against fixed policies—can automate the build-test-improve modeling cycle. Think AlphaEvolve for forecasting problems.

*Sample-Efficient General Models*

Today’s forecasting models are narrowly crafted with deep human priors. But larger models will outperform state-of-the-art specialized models.

Unlike existing event models, our models leverage data from across contexts and rely less on human intuition. And compared to LLMs, our models are built with more inductive priors and rely more heavily on inference-time compute—improving sample efficiency.

*Why It Matters*

In the real economy, our models could be useful for forecasting supply chain volatility, energy supply and demand, even earthquake risk.

Science is, Ian Hacking writes, the taming of chance. It is the process of iteratively updating priors (something like: identify uncertainty, conceive experiment to reduce uncertainty, execute, update). If science is uncertainty-reduction, forecasting is a critical measure of progress. 

Better forecasting improves our ability to select interesting experiments (roughly those with greatest expected uncertainty reduction) and update priors. Our models will be used by labs and academics in data-heavy domains. 

Sam's ex-girlfriend introduced him to Greg back at Carnegie Mellon in 2017, and while that relationship didn't last, their friendship has. After college, Greg went to Harvard Law School, while Sam worked for three years at Jane Street on their Options desk, building & leading a satellite dev team.

The bottleneck is operating the hardware. Today, engineers spend days or weeks by hand to bring a chip to operating conditions for just two qubits. A qubit is the information-carrying unit of a quantum computer, the equivalent of a bit in a classical one, and a useful machine needs billions. 

Removing the human from that loop is only half the problem. Every command an AI sends to a quantum computer must be optimised for the specific hardware it runs on.

oneLiner: Agentic platform for predictive neuro drug discovery + data foundry.
description:
We are developing therapies for disorders driven by dysfunctional neural circuits. To develop these therapies, we are building an agentic discovery platform that learns from experiments in our own in vivo lab.

Our agents use CircuitATLAS to connect disease phenotypes with the neural circuits, cell types and molecular mechanisms, identify therapeutic targets and design experiments to test them. Our cross-species models learn from large-scale neural activity data to identify conserved circuit states and help predict how an intervention’s effects may translate from preclinical models to humans.

At our Data Foundry in Manila, our team of RAs test these hypotheses in vitro and in vivo. The results refine our models and guide the next set of experiments. This lab-in-the-loop approach allows our agents to develop and test ideas against experimental evidence throughout discovery.

We are starting with epilepsy, with the goal of developing first-in-class therapies across a full spectrum of disorders driven by dysfunctional brain activity.

Publications:

- CircuitATLAS (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09643). Target discovery platform which combines mechanistic reasoning with an in vivo lab-in-the-loop. AI agents identify therapeutic targets and design experiments that our research teams execute in the lab. The resulting biological data feeds back into the discovery process to iteratively refine hypotheses and validate new interventions.

- Cross species representation learning (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11222). Aligning mouse and human neural activity to predict clinical drug efficacy from preclinical data.

oneLiner: The deterministic layer for frontier intelligence
description:
CTGT is an applied AI research laboratory fundamentally solving the alignment and reliability bottleneck for enterprise AI.

For enterprises, especially highly regulated industries, deploying Generative AI is historically a compromise between capability and catastrophic risk. Standard enterprise approaches, such as RAG, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering, operate at the wrong abstraction layer. They are inherently probabilistic, carry massive engineering overhead, and fail to deliver the mathematical certainty required by the Fortune 500.

We focus on the science of representation engineering and have productized mechanistic interpretability. By opening the "black box" of neural networks, CTGT has developed a proprietary architecture that intervenes directly at the model's representation layer. We convert complex corporate SOPs, SEC/FINRA regulations, and strict editorial rulebooks into machine-readable "Policy as Code," enforcing deterministic constraints and defensible audit trails without requiring expensive model retraining.

The result is a step-function breakthrough in enterprise AI economics and capability. Our fundamental architecture allows organizations to run secure, self-hosted open-source models that mathematically match the reasoning and performance of frontier models. Benchmarks from our enterprise deployments demonstrate a 96.5% prevention of hallucinations, up to a 3.3× accuracy multiplier in complex domain-specific tasks, and an 80-90% reduction in human-in-the-loop manual review.

Backed by an $8M seed round from Gradient Ventures (Google), General Catalyst, and Y Combinator, CTGT is currently deployed with Fortune 500 companies, including Tier-1 financial institutions and global media conglomerates, giving them the deterministic control necessary to deploy enterprise AI with zero margin for error.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐰𝐞 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬:
I (Angel) have had three knee surgeries since my mid-teens and was billed more than $250K for care that should have cost a fraction of that. Fighting those inflated charges was so painful that we set out to build a consumer-facing AI agent to do it for others. In less than five months, we helped sixty patients erase or reduce over $300K from their medical bills.

This inspired us to fix the problem farther upstream: stopping bad payments before the patient ever sees a bill. So we launched payment integrity, machine-learning models that audit every medical claim for self-insured employers and health plans in real time.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦:
• Self-insured employers waste $60 B+ each year on claims that never should have been paid. Healthcare is the 2nd largest company expense after payroll.

• Manual audits are slow and partial: Reviewers focus only on high-dollar claims, letting millions more slip through unnoticed.

• Existing audit software is static: Decades-old rule engines can’t keep pace with evolving codes, contracts, or billing tactics.

• Incentives are misaligned: Third-party administrators are paid to process claims, not to police them, so accuracy checks are minimal.

𝐎𝐮𝐫 𝐒𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:
Our models audit medical claims before and after payments have been issued. We catch nuanced billing, coding, and contract errors to save 3-7% on annual claims spend. We work with self-insured employers and health plans.

𝐀𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐔𝐬:
Angel Onuoha (CEO) and Ahmad Shehu (CTO) have worked together for 4 years. Before Avelis Health they built Zuvy, a Lagos-based fintech company that provided invoice factoring to small businesses. Zuvy was acquired by The BAS Group in 2025.

oneLiner: AI rebuilt coding. We’re rebuilding the phone
description:
AI changed coding when it got its own environment instead of a chat window. Developers stopped typing every line and started handing off whole tasks. The phone is next, and it needs the same rebuild.

Blue is that rebuild: a phone that’s also your chief of staff. It reads every notification, text, and email for you. Anything else is one button away: say what needs doing, and Blue gets it done in the background, using the right apps.

It knows you from day one. Switch from your iPhone and Blue brings over your apps, messages, photos, and passwords, so it already knows who matters to you, how you write, and which card to use. No logins to hand over, no context to explain.

An app can’t do this; it takes owning the phone. Blue runs our own OS on Google Pixel today, with our own hardware in development. We sold out our first batch at YC’s Alumni Demo Day in September.

The team brings complementary experience at scale: Omar Abdelaziz led Google Assistant’s transition to LLMs and holds one of the earliest patents in LLM-based computer control; Peter Krogh spent decades designing voice-first dialog systems and before Blue was a design lead at Google DeepMind building actions for Gemini Live; Muhammad Farhan Hossain helped ship Apple Vision Pro, is named on dozens of hardware and systems patents, and has led products from prototype to mass production.

oneLiner: Zero-trust authentication, authorization, and auditing for AI agents
description:
The agentic era is here, but its foundation is dangerously insecure. A growing number of high-profile "AI agent gone rogue" security incidents make headlines each week.

As enterprise adoption of agentic software has far outpaced the development of applicable cybersecurity solutions, CISOs have loudly voiced a growing need for verifiable, fine-grained security controls on complex multi-agent systems. That's why we built Multifactor.

Multifactor offers best-in-class authentication, authorization, and auditing technologies for agentic systems, allowing users to securely and revocably share online accounts with agents while maintaining fine-grained permissions and a detailed event history. A world-class "account manager" that allows agents to securely use online accounts on your behalf is just the start—our early enterprise partners include companies using AI agents to manage $7.5+ billion manufacturing supply chains, where the consequences for lapses in security are severe. Our patented AI security technology seamlessly integrates with existing agentic software to thwart attacks like prompt injection, so CISOs and end users alike can breathe a sigh of relief, without slowing the pace of AI adoption.

oneLiner: Building AGI that can innovate.
description:
Ndea is building frontier AI systems that blend intuitive pattern recognition and formal reasoning into a unified architecture.

# AI for Scientific Advancement

Unlike all life before us, humanity's ascent is a story of ingenuity, not just biological evolution. Our progress has been driven by the curiosity to acquire knowledge, the ability to pass it on, and an intrinsic drive to innovate. We build technology which gives us leverage beyond our biology.

We stand at the top of a knowledge and technology colossus that we collectively created over the past ten thousand generations. Scientific progress has helped us overcome burdens that long defined human life — famines, plagues, and widespread illiteracy. Science will continue to redefine the boundaries of the human condition.

Today, the acceleration of scientific progress hinges on one factor: AI capable of independent invention and discovery. This capacity is the gateway to advancements beyond our wildest imagination.

# A New Research Lab

We're starting Ndea — an AI research and science lab. The name - like 'idea' with an 'n' - is inspired by the Greek concepts ennoia (intuitive understanding) and dianoia (logical reasoning), capturing our first goal to merge deep learning with program synthesis.

Ndea is entirely focused on developing and operationalizing AGI to realize unprecedented scientific progress in our lifetime for the benefit of all current and future generations.

Building AGI alone is a monumental undertaking, but our mission is even bigger. We're creating a factory for rapid scientific advancement — a factory capable of inventing and commercializing N ideas.

From our vantage point today, we see many 'known' frontiers like self-driving vehicles, drug discovery, sustainable energy, robotics, and space exploration. While AGI will benefit all of these, the most exciting adventure lies in the 'unknown'. AGI promises discoveries and progress we cannot imagine today.

Today that is two products: Phenotyping, which measures every fish for shape, size and condition and links it to its family for breeding decisions, and Digital Twin, which places cameras on processing lines and farm sites onto the floor plan with live views, automatic counts and a built-in AI assistant.

The same per-fish measurements are the foundation for Plant Robotics: robot cells that handle whole fish on the processing line, working alongside the people there. Fish are wet, slippery, soft and never the same twice, which is exactly why this work is still manual and why it needs measurement-driven robots built for food plants rather than rigid grippers and tabletop demos. We are now selecting processing plants for the first pilots on real lines.

We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, and every deployment adds labeled images to a proprietary multi-species dataset that improves our models across species and becomes the brain for autonomous seafood production.

oneLiner: Agentic AI for intellectual property

oneLiner: Trade with superhuman instinct

oneLiner: Agent Platform for Life Sciences

Chetan started his career as a research engineer, but quickly realized he enjoyed building more than research. He joined EvolutionaryScale as their sole founding product engineer, launching their developer-scientist platform and scaling to tens of thousands of users and billions of API calls. oneLiner: AI video editor (raw footage into finished videos)
description:
Cardboard (cardboard.ai) is an AI video editor that turns raw footage into finished videos, from social clips and highlight reels to product demos, launch videos and event recaps. Describe the video you want, and Cardboard turns your clips, photos, recordings or a link into an edit you can watch, change and export, in the browser, in the Mac app, or right inside ChatGPT and Claude. It pulls out the best moments, removes pauses and filler words, adds captions, titles, music and B-roll, and reframes for Reels, Shorts and TikTok. It’s built for marketing teams, founders and creators who need video every week without learning a timeline.

Say what you need, like “three 30-second ad variants” or “a customer testimonial from these interviews”, and Cardboard’s AI agent, Director, builds a first cut in minutes. You refine it by chatting or on a full timeline, with your team. Cardboard edits the footage you already have. Unlike AI video generators such as Runway or Sora, it doesn’t create new video from a text prompt.

- Recreate the style of a reference video with your own footage.
- Make motion graphics from a prompt, from animated titles to 3D scenes like a spinning product shot.
- Cut to the beat, with match cuts, transitions and effects synced to the music.
- 80+ ready-made recipes (templates) for videos like launch videos, product showcases, podcast clips, webinar highlights, and testimonials.
- Export the finished video, or hand the timeline off to Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Why now: AI models can finally understand video, and WebGPU makes a professional editor possible in a browser tab. Most AI video tools are either an old editor with AI bolted on, or an agent with no real editor behind it. Cardboard is built to be both.

Team: Saksham Aggarwal (CEO) and Ishan Sharma (CTO) have been friends for 15 years, since school. Saksham studied computer science at BITS Pilani, was co-founder and CTO of Iterate AI (backed by Entrepreneur First), and worked in growth at Sequoia-backed Flint. Ishan spent nearly five years building performance-critical browser apps at HackerRank (YC S11), and at 14 built Hotspoter, a Windows app with over 5 million downloads.

Together, they are unusually suited to build the editor core others avoid.

Video is becoming the default distribution channel, and the team that iterates fastest compounds attention. Cardboard becomes the default workspace for video production, the way Canva/Figma became the workspace for design - because it’s collaborative, fast, and does the tedious parts for you.

(formerly usecardboard.com or cardboard.sh)

oneLiner: Frontier AI Defenses for Social Engineering Attacks

BeeSafe changes that by deploying undercover AI agents that engage attackers directly, expose hidden infrastructure, and convert live adversarial conversations into actionable intelligence. Each engagement adds to BeeSafe's proprietary dataset of real attacker behavior and trains foundational models that continually learn about counter-persuasion, deception, and manipulation in the wild.

BeeSafe is starting in financial crime, where banks already value our data against Authorized Push Payment (APP) fraud and money laundering, but the opportunity is far broader. The same data and models that uncover mule networks today can protect consumers, secure enterprises, and strengthen governments against the next generation of AI-powered social engineering attacks tomorrow.

oneLiner: We help software companies get discovered and used by AI agents
description:
Scope is the system companies use to measure and improve how agents discover, interact and use their product.

As more products gets used through AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar agents, agents are starting to influence which tools get chosen, how they get set up, and whether they keep getting used. Most companies still cannot see that process clearly.

We run real workflows across agents and show teams when the agent picks them versus a competitor, where it breaks, where docs or product surfaces confuse the agent, and what to change to get better results and a better agent experience.

oneLiner: Extrapolative AI to unlock First-in-Class drugs
description:
We’re an AI-native biotech, working on replacing needles with pills. Many drugs, like insulin or Ozempic, are wonderful except you have to inject them. Because the pills operate on biology which has been shown to be effective in people, rather than merely in animal models of disease, we avoid what has historically been the single biggest risk in drug discovery.  This should dramatically increase our probability of success.

There’s $200B of treatable diseases and validated human biology without a pill because discovery programs lack a tractable chemical starting point. This is a zero-shot inference problem, because these targets have no training data, so LLMs and other historical interpolative AI approaches are insufficient. Instead, we are building our own extrapolative frontier models that reason beyond their training data. Most critically, we have repeatedly validated our platform on both our own and partner programs. On 4 biologically- and structurally-diverse targets where we had zero training data, we successfully picked binders that were validated experimentally, with confirmation ranging from primary screen hits to crystallographic structures.

oneLiner: Agents that own the work
description:
AI chatbots can answer questions, but they can't do your work — they aren't connected to your tools, can't take actions, and stop running when you close the tab. Meanwhile, knowledge workers are still spending most of their day switching between dozens of SaaS apps, manually stitching together workflows that should be automated.

Tasklet is the AI agent that actually does the work. It connects to every tool you use — via thousands of built-in integrations, any HTTP API, or MCP servers — and takes real actions on your behalf: pulling reports, updating CRMs, triaging emails, processing data, and more. When it needs a UI, it generates one on the fly. When it needs to crunch numbers or do bulk operations, it writes and runs code in a cloud sandbox. When it needs to interact with a website that doesn't have an API, it uses a real browser. And because it runs in the cloud 24/7, you can set up triggers to have it take ongoing responsibility for workflows — not just do something once, but handle it going forward.

The product is deliberately simple: a chat interface where you talk to an extremely capable agent. But underneath that simplicity is a cloud-native agent runtime, best-in-class context engineering, a universal connections layer, and multi-model support that keeps us on the frontier as AI improves. 

We think legacy SaaS is being unbundled by agents, and Tasklet is the operating system that ties it all together.

oneLiner: Engineering the future of Cancer Drug Discovery
description:
NxtCure Labs is an AI-native, full-stack CRO built to take therapeutics from discovery to market faster. We are reinventing medicine from lab to drug discovery.

About 2 million Americans are diagnosed with cancer every year. Science has never moved faster, new immunotherapies, targeted drugs and cancer vaccines arrive every year. But roughly 90% of cancer drugs fail in clinical trials, and about 80% of trials run late. The breakthroughs exist. The way we test them is stuck in the last century.

NxtCure is building autonomous clinical trials. Before a single patient enrolls, we run the trial thousands of times on digital twins. Each virtual patient is a system of coupled differential equations that track how a drug moves through plasma, tumor and heart, and how the tumor grows, shrinks or fights back. The parameters are fit to real trial data, so every twin behaves like real biology. Across thousands of simulations we can calculate the odds that a dose will hit its endpoints, and fix the protocol before it costs anyone time, money or hope.

Then 13 AI agents run the trial. Each one owns a stage: drafting the protocol, ranking sites, pre-screening patients, forecasting drug supply, watching for adverse events, predicting dropout, cleaning data and writing the final report. As real data comes in, the twins update and flag problems weeks before a human would see them.

In 2025, the FDA laid out how computer simulation can take its place. Soon a cancer drug will run through thousands of simulated trials before it ever touches a lab, and reach patients years faster. We’re building that future.

oneLiner: agents for the rest of us

Take life personally.

Text and selected context can be sent through Moonshot's server to a model when the app needs to understand a moment. Nothing leaves without your yes. The privacy policy explains every data path, stored copy, permission, and deletion control in detail.

Moonshot is in early access. Join the waitlist to hear when access opens, read more about the team and product on the About page, or use the Contact page for a direct written response from the Moonshot team.

Let's make it a Moonshot.

oneLiner: A multiplayer discovery workspace for human and agentic scientists
description:
A new agent, tool, or generative model alone doesn’t solve the whole problem for most research questions. Someone still has to assemble the data, work out which methods to use and get the tools and datasets working together. We’re building Noto, a multiplayer discovery workbench for human and agentic scientists, to bring everyone's favorite frontier models, agents, tools, and scientific models into one shared workspace, so that you can focus on making your next discovery, rather than wrestling with your Python environment or finding GPUs.

Plan an experiment, work with its generated data, run an analysis or model, maybe even train a new model, and keep the results in the notebook. We designed Noto so that the inputs, code, methods and results stay connected across local and hosted compute. Both people and agents need to see how a result was produced and build on it. Biology is where we’re starting, with the workbench being built for more general research across many scientific disciplines.

Available now: our first biological analysis tools, hosted model inference, and an initial agent interface. Free usage is available within limits, alongside paid model runs and individual and team plans. Researchers can run sequence and structure analyses and hosted scientific models without provisioning GPUs or maintaining each model’s dependencies.

In development: the full multiplayer notebook and wider agent workflows and integrations.

Orikata Bio Public Benefit Corporation, or Orikata Bio PBC, is the company. We work under two brands: Orikata Bio for biological discovery and Megure Labs for scientific software.

Biological discovery with Orikata Bio

We’re developing Ibuki, a world-model family for biology, to learn how evolution, sequence, structure and function relate and use those relationships to understand and engineer living systems. We’re pretraining our own protein language models, and developing coordinate and multimodal models for prediction, inverse folding, alignment and generative design. Proteins are our starting point; DNA, RNA, small molecules, and other biological modalities are part of the longer-term direction.

Along the way, we assembled Umi, with over 100 billion unique protein sequences, and Sora, with nearly two billion protein structure records. Having that much data only helps if we can organize it, compare it and find the biology relevant to a particular question. We’re building the full-corpus embedding, indexing and customer access that will bring more of those collections into research workflows.

Our key insight was that the fixed substitution tables used to compare biological sequences are the simplest example of a neural network. Replacing them with contextual substitution operators lets us learn how positions correspond, from reference alignments and directly from molecular geometry. Hikoboshi (open source) turns those learned relationships into tools for sequence and structure alignment, search, clustering and many other evolutionary analysis pipelines.
GitHub: https://github.com/orikata-bio/hikoboshi

Scientific software with Megure Labs

Learning those relationships meant making the alignment calculation itself trainable. Orihime (open source), our differentiable-alignment and structured-attention library, lets neural networks learn through scientific algorithms on CPUs and GPUs. It supplies the training machinery behind our learned alignment methods.
GitHub: https://github.com/megure-labs/orihime

Running the models efficiently is its own problem. Hataya (private evaluation), our inference engine and compiler for scientific models, turns trained models and their dependencies into standalone CPU and GPU programs, carrying the exact weights, identity and verification evidence with them. We’re building it to make both our models and public scientific models cheaper to run, including through Noto’s hosted service.

Kaname coordinates long-running agent work across every model provider: tasks, compute, permissions, retries and the record of what happened. We’re bringing that coordination and provenance into Noto’s research workflows so work can continue across people, agents and machines.

Researchers can start with a single analysis or hosted model run today. Noto is where we’re bringing them together so an analysis or model run can become part of a continuing research project, with the data, methods and results kept alongside it.

Try Noto’s live tools: https://megure.ai/noto/workspace/
Biological tools: https://orikata.ai/tools/
Scientific software: https://megure.ai/
Biological discovery: https://orikata.ai/
Open source: https://github.com/megure-labs and https://github.com/orikata-bio
For research use, questions about the data or private evaluations: casey@orikata.ai

Glen does more. You can query the original agent behind any line of code, or search every session your org has ever run. It distills what your team does into skills and surfaces the right one automatically. Agents work multiplayer, picking up the style and context of whoever else is on the file. oneLiner: Making chemicals 100,000x faster
description:
We build foundational AI models for chemistry. Almost nothing you buy is a single chemical. Products like datacenter coolant, GPU thermal paste, paint, and glue are formulations, which are mixtures of around ten ingredients each, and demand for them has grown quickly because of AI and EVs.

Designing a new formulation is essentially a search problem, because there are more possible mixtures than anyone could ever test, and none of them can be predicted in advance. As a result, bringing a single formulation to market today takes three to five years of trial and error in a lab.

Our models predict how a mixture will behave far faster than the standard methods used today, which lets us design new formulations in weeks rather than years, at a fraction of the cost. To prove this, we used them to invent three chemicals that never existed before, including a PFAS-free coolant for datacenters, and we have since synthesized and patented all three.

We are already working with some of the largest manufacturers to design formulations for them, and we are building our own lab to generate the data that will train our next models.

oneLiner: A factory for small and specialized video reasoning models
description:
The world generates petabytes of video every day, and almost none of it is readable to machines.  Frontier VLMs that can unlock this (like Gemini) are too expensive to run at the volume real industries have, too generic for any single task, and can't be deployed on-prem where sensitive video lives.

We are building an auto vision factory: take video plus a customer's objective, distill a frontier model, and post-train a small open model that is SOTA on that one task and serve it blazingly fast. Our first product, Marlin, is a 2B-parameter open-weights video VLM that matches Gemini-2.5-flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding at a fraction of the cost.

oneLiner: RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time
description:
Reific builds RL environments for superhuman reasoning over time, for the frontier labs that train agents. AI has learned to reason over text and code. But most of what matters in the real world shows up as numbers that change every second: a heartbeat, a gearbox, a GPU cluster. No human can track thousands of signals at once, but AI should be able to.

In our environments, data streams in on a clock while the agent works, and every action is graded by what actually happened. Most AI training today teaches models to match human experts. We treat human performance as the floor. Each environment comes from real, de-identified records, in three task families: personal agents, industry, and science & compute.

Today, even the best frontier model averages under 50% on each family. oneLiner: Virtual machines for long-running agents
description:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

oneLiner: AI-powered blood test to detect cancer in dogs (and cats soon).
description:
Canos is bringing a human-grade liquid biopsy platform for dogs, starting with a single blood draw. We sequence cell-free DNA to perform multi-modal analysis of fragmentation, copy number variation, native methylation (5mC and 5hmC) and more to detect cancer signals. Owners bank a healthy baseline for their dog and track changes every year. Dogs already diagnosed get personalized monitoring through treatment. We partner with mobile vets and vet clinics to serve SF and NYC. 

Our mission is to make pet cancer curable through early detection and monitoring.

oneLiner: 100% automated inspection for precision hardware parts
description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

oneLiner: The Microsoft of the AI era: the operating system for AI agents.
description:
Tilo gives AI agents one shared computer. Today every agent gets its own virtual machine and works by screenshots and clicks, which is slow, expensive and brittle. Agents that work together have to describe what they did to each other in messages.

Tilo is a Linux-based operating system built for agents as users. Every app exports typed actions that agents call over MCP while people use the same actions as buttons, on the same live state. Many agents work in one workspace at once and read each other's work instead of messaging about it. Every change is attributed and can be undone, and irreversible actions need permission. Because state and interface are separate, agents can generate an app's entire UI on demand.

On the same multi-app task with the same model, agents on Tilo were about 29× cheaper and 90× faster than computer use, which failed. A small model on Tilo did it for about 1/10,000 of the frontier model's cost. In our scale test, 50 agents worked in one shared workspace on a single laptop, at about 60 MB of memory per agent. Tilo runs headless, in our cloud, or as a desktop, and you can open any workspace from the browser.

oneLiner: Expert AI agents that explore, understand, and verify mobile apps.
description:
AI made building apps fast. Verifying did not keep up: every mobile team, from a first release to a billion downloads, still waits on QA, design, accessibility, compliance and security checks for everything it builds.

Aucert is a team of expert AI agents that does that work in hours, with no scripts. Each agent explores the app on its own, learns how it should work, and finds the issues in its area. Aucert plugs into agentic coding workflows, so developers and coding agents fix issues in the same loop, on every build.

Live: Accessibility · Google Play policy
Beta: Validation (functional QA) · Design
Coming soon: Apple App Store policy · Security · Create your own

oneLiner: OpenAI for Financial Markets
description: Mnemonic Labs (YC F26) is a neolab founded by two brothers who are Olympiad finalists and MIT graduates; Kalki made $20M in annual PnL at 22 at Tower and Videh was the youngest quant at Citadel at 19. Just as LLMs and scaling laws quickly dominated all other NLP approaches, we're building world models that will dominate both human and machine traders.

oneLiner: The managed cloud for AI agents.
description: Maritime is a fully managed cloud platform for startups selling AI agents. We help them run thousands of agents, each in its own isolated, persistent computer, starting at $1 per agent per month, with all underlying infrastructure, scaling, sleep/wake, and monitoring handled automatically.

oneLiner: Caller ID for Voice AI
description: DeepMark is the authentication layer for AI voice. When an AI agent speaks, we embed a compact, machine-readable ID directly into the audio, not in metadata, which gets stripped the moment a file is touched. The ID resolves to a trust record, so a bank, a call center, or the person on the line can verify in real time who the agent is.

oneLiner: A shared drive for your team and all your AI agents.
description:
Our mission is to rebuild the file system, the oldest idea in computing, for its newest users: AI agents.

FlashDrive is a shared drive for teams and their AI agents. You can use it via MCP or mount it like a normal folder on macOS and Linux, so your laptop, your teammates' and every sandbox work in the same live files at once. Agents hand off work through files: one writes, the next one reads.

That makes AI multiplayer across a whole company. Everyone keeps the agent they already like, whether that's Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or something custom, and there's no new app to learn. Your agents and your teammates' agents work in the same files and pick up where each other left off.

Shared drives were built for people. Agents work differently: many of them edit the same files at once. Unlike Dropbox or Google Drive, FlashDrive merges edits made at the same time, or keeps both, instead of creating a conflicted copy. Cloud sandboxes connect with no setup, huge files stream instead of filling the disk, and every file can be searched with keywords and grep.

(FlashDrive is by Evokoa, Inc.)

oneLiner: Travel Search & Booking Infrastructure for AI agents
Documents of the future: the collaboration surface for people and…
description:
Agents now write faster than anyone can read. Spacesheep is where their work lands: any agent turns a session's output into a space that your team takes in at a glance. It works with the agents you already use, and has its own agent built in.

Teams work on it together: comment on the exact spot, @mention a teammate, or ask @spacesheep and an agent makes the change live on every screen. Every change is a version, and every space is searchable by meaning, for people and agents alike. Spaces can show live data streamed from servers and sensors, and connect to the tools your team already uses.

Teams use it for research, design docs, dashboards, slides and internal apps.

oneLiner: An AI coach for every employee!
description:
ChampionEffect is an AI Coach that teaches AI to every employee at a company, in Slack and Teams.

The Coach helps with a new AI concept, a new workflow, or any tool. It jumps on a call and walks you through the work, just like a coworker would. It points to the top use cases in your industry and tailors everything to your company’s needs and tools. Every time someone does a walkthrough with the Coach, it learns how real work gets done at the company and uses that knowledge with other coworkers.

Before this, we ran a YC company (Cambly) that taught English to millions of professionals and generated $100M+ in revenue. Now we’re using what we learned to teach millions about AI.

oneLiner: Applied AI for Enterprise GTM (3x founders, 10x growth, backed by ANT)
description:
Gather's AI agent for enterprise GTM continually interviews real buyers and turns those conversations into content that drives pipeline and simulations that predict customer behavior.

More than 65 enterprise marketing teams, including Envoy, Eclypsium, Cover Genius, Fortinet, CoStar, Bagel Brands, and Family Express, use Gather to create original, on-brand, third-party validated thought leadership, reports, ebooks, and campaign content.

That customer understanding compounds with every interview. Our models draw on quantitative, qualitative, and voice data from over 300,000 real interviews across customers, with thousands added monthly. Teams can simulate how buyers will respond to messaging, pricing, and market shifts, with supporting evidence and a confidence level behind every answer. When confidence is low, Gather automatically runs new research.

We’re starting by replacing research firms and content agencies. We’re building the intelligence enterprises and their agents need to understand and serve customers, whether human or AI.

Built by the team that created Cooliris (acquired by Yahoo) and Pulse (acquired by Gartner), and ran Gartner Peer Insights.

oneLiner: Structured products on prediction markets
description: DataNode is building the structuring data layer for event risk. Our engine combines prediction markets with traditional derivatives to quantify and risk assess any event exposure and build a priced, tailored hedge, even before a market for it exists.

oneLiner: AI CEO that leads human & agent teams on company-wide missions
description:
Luminary is an AI CEO that leads human and agent teams on company-wide missions. We're building the complete infrastructure for a fully AI-native company, starting with a world model of how your business works and building up to an AI CEO that can lead it.

Today's AI tools are good at automating the work they're handed, but they still wait to be told what to do next. So even with the abundance of AI agents, companies are still bottlenecked by leadership and vision. Someone has to decide what's worth building, rally the right people behind it, and bring it to market.

Luminary takes on that job. Instead of asking it to build a feature, you hand it part of your business to grow. It then proactively discovers opportunities, plans high-impact missions, and leads your people and its own agent swarms to accomplish them. 

Some examples of audacious missions it can execute:

- Launch a product: It spots customers building the same workaround, makes the business case, directs coding agents to build it, and rolls it out.
- Enter a new market: It finds an unexpected group of buyers, reworks positioning and pricing around them, and wins the first accounts.
- Rescue a stalled deal: It notices an enterprise deal losing momentum, designs a new strategy with your sales team, and gets it signed.

Under the hood, Luminary builds a living world model and follows a leadership constitution that shapes every call. Proprietary evals check every deliverable, and a recursive self-improvement loop turns each mission into institutional wisdom.
